if: the inward supply is a VESSEL OR AIRCRAFT

AND it is NOT used for making a taxable supply of (A) further supply of such vessels or aircraft, (B) transportation of passengers, (C) imparting training on navigating such vessels, or (D) imparting training on flying such aircraft
AND it is NOT used for transportation of goods
then: input tax credit is NOT AVAILABLE on that vessel or aircraft
note: Unlike clause (a), this clause has no seating threshold — every vessel and aircraft is caught unless an exception applies. It carries one exception clause (a) does not: transportation of GOODS. A cargo aircraft or freight vessel therefore escapes the block, while a company jet used for staff travel does not. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this clause; later amendments are not held locally.
